        "Full owned152-line three-path diff read. Shared HandleMultipleAttachments now rejects a selection if any URL is disallowed. It computes canDetach from message policy and every attachment having a file and not already external/detached. Detach/delete return when false; save remains separate. This original all-or-nothing selection behavior differs from fixed current code, which filters unavailable/disallowed/external entries then checks message policy. Do not project later partial-selection support onto this landing.",
        "AttachmentListController keeps generic delete and shift-delete supported/enabled and handles them through HandleSelectedAttachments. Shared action policy returns without modifying disallowed content. Disabling the attachment command is not equivalent to this consumed action: historical author reports that dispatch would try a later controller and delete the message. Exact comm source establishes supported/enabled dispatch plus guarded action; no unpaired engine controller implementation or runtime fallthrough result is a public premise.",
        "CanDetachAttachments is documented as message-level policy, distinct from per-attachment deleted/detached state. It short-circuits missing folder, Newsgroup and offline IMAP before S/MIME regex and OpenPGP helper. OpenPGP helper masks PGP_MIME_SIGNED/PGP_MIME_ENCRYPTED when status flags exist. This is about the actual displayed message security state, not whether an unsigned reply quotes a signed ancestor. Source regex remains unanchored/case-sensitive as written; no broader MIME parser claim.",
        "Changed test adds attachment-bar click, VK_DELETE and waitForTick to an existing standalone wrapper/attached encrypted-message scenario. It then opens the attachment in a new message window and directly asserts body and parent/child security icons. This is indirect continued-openability coverage, not a direct assertion of attachment/message count or every signed/encrypted stored-message case. Standalone-file loading also meets the missing-folder restriction. Fixed selected test now uses KEY_Delete, a later change separate from owned original. All inspected direct assertions have nonempty expected messages; missing should alone in existing messages is not a defect.",
